source.title: Raman Spectroscopy of Graphene & Graphene Oxide
source.note: Atlas fields are verbatim copies of the PEAKS, RATIOS, CHEAT and REFS constants. Blocks named match / fit / matchDefaults / fitDefaults / referenceExcitation / ratioMap are app data derived from or added to the atlas, and say so.

referenceExcitation.note: The atlas does not state an excitation wavelength for its positions. 532 nm was chosen by the atlas author (2026-10-02) as the reference for dispersion-shifting match windows. App setting, not atlas data.

matchDefaults.note: App settings, not atlas data. A peak matches a band if it lies within the band's atlas range ± toleranceCm (after dispersion shift). Bands with dispersion.widenWindow get an extra ± allowance × |ΔE| because the atlas gives no rate for them; 50 cm⁻¹/eV is the atlas D-band rate, used as a generous envelope.

fitDefaults.note: App settings, not atlas data: bounds for the deconvolution fitter. Centres are bounded to each band's match window so bands cannot swap places.

atlasNotes.title: Raman Spectroscopy of Graphene & Graphene Oxide
atlasNotes.subtitle: An interactive atlas of the nine-band deconvolution model. Click any peak in the spectrum or a tab below to explore its vibrational origin, the physics it encodes, and how to use it diagnostically — cross-checked against the primary literature.
atlasNotes.banner: This atlas uses the graphene-oxide 9-band deconvolution. The second-order G* (D+D″) band is placed at its correct ~2450 cm⁻¹ position (matching your measured data); the ~2850–2920 cm⁻¹ region is sp³ C–H stretching, not a lattice phonon band. Corrected / updated items carry a red note and references.
atlasNotes.referencesNote: Citation counts (badges) are from Semantic Scholar, retrieved Jul 2026 — Google Scholar figures are typically higher. Every source is well cited; the foundational reviews exceed several thousand citations, confirming reputability. Green badges mark ≥2,000 citations.
atlasNotes.footer:
Built for reference use. Peak positions are representative and shift with excitation wavelength, strain, doping, layer number and oxidation degree — always calibrate against a known standard.
Sources are hyperlinked above; ■ marks references added during the accuracy review.

bands.label: D*
bands.name: D* band (Sadezky D4)
bands.process: Not a graphene double-resonance mode. Attributed to the disordered sp³-rich phase and the phonon density of states of finite/defective domains.
bands.mechanism: C–H in-plane bending, vibrations of short aliphatic / polyene-like (trans-polyacetylene-type) chains, and sp³-rich carbon adjacent to oxygen functional groups. In Sadezky's five-band scheme for disordered carbon this is the D4 component.
bands.meaning: A direct marker of sp³ functionalisation and edge C–H / C–O bonding. Grows with oxidation and shrinks during chemical/thermal reduction as the sp² network is restored. Frequently too weak to fit reliably in well-ordered or lightly oxidised GO.
bands.diagnostics: Presence/area tracks oxidation degree. Its disappearance is one signature of successful reduction toward rGO.

dispersion.source: not a double-resonance band in the atlas; treated as non-dispersive

fit.source: atlas plot.sig × 2.3548 — the atlas's schematic curve width, used only as a starting value for deconvolution (the atlas gives no measured FWHM)

bands.label: D
bands.name: D band (disorder / defect)
bands.use: Defect density; crystallite size Lₐ / inter-defect distance L_D
bands.process: Intervalley double resonance (K↔K′): one in-plane transverse-optical (iTO) phonon near the K point plus one elastic scattering event off a defect. Strongly dispersive (~50 cm⁻¹ per eV of laser energy).
bands.mechanism: Symmetric A₁g breathing mode of the six-membered aromatic rings. Because it needs a defect (or edge) to conserve momentum, it is forbidden in pristine, infinite single-layer graphene.
bands.meaning: The workhorse defect probe. I<sub>D</sub>/I<sub>G</sub> quantifies defect density and crystallite size — but only once you know which regime you are in (see the ratio guide: low-defect Tuinstra–Koenig vs. high-defect amorphisation).
bands.diagnostics: Lₐ (nm) = (560/E<sub>l</sub>⁴)·(I<sub>D</sub>/I<sub>G</sub>)⁻¹ in the low-defect regime (E<sub>l</sub> in eV; Cançado 2011). Also yields inter-defect distance L_D.

dispersion.source: atlas D.process: "Strongly dispersive (~50 cm⁻¹ per eV of laser energy)"

fit.source: atlas plot.sig × 2.3548 — the atlas's schematic curve width, used only as a starting value for deconvolution (the atlas gives no measured FWHM)

bands.label: D″
bands.name: D″ band (Sadezky D3)
bands.process: Broad feature between D and G, fit as the D3 component of disordered carbon.
bands.mechanism: Amorphous sp² carbon and interstitial lattice defects, plus out-of-plane vibrations of oxygen functional groups (epoxy C–O–C, hydroxyl C–OH). Reflects lattice distortion by oxygen intercalants.
bands.meaning: Its intensity/width scales with the amorphous fraction; it decreases and narrows during thermal annealing as the lattice recrystallises.
bands.diagnostics: Useful for staging oxidation/reduction. Often small (undetectable) in well-crystalline flakes.
bands.correction: The label D″ is overloaded. Here it denotes the ~1500 cm⁻¹ amorphous band (Sadezky D3). In mainstream graphene physics, D″ instead denotes a ~1100 cm⁻¹ phonon on the LA branch — the one that produces the ~2450 cm⁻¹ combination band (see the D+D″ tab). Keep the two meanings distinct when comparing papers.

bands.label: G
bands.name: G band (graphitic E₂g)
bands.origin: E₂g in-plane C–C stretch at Γ
bands.use: Baseline mode; oxidation / doping / strain gauge
bands.process: First-order, Raman-allowed at the Brillouin-zone centre (Γ). No defect required — active in every sp² carbon material.
bands.mechanism: In-plane bond-stretching of sp² C–C atom pairs (the degenerate LO/iTO optical mode of E₂g symmetry at Γ). The fundamental reference peak of the spectrum.
bands.meaning: Blue-shifts (stiffens) upon oxidation as sp² domains become isolated, and is sensitive to charge doping (via removal of the Kohn anomaly) and strain (splits into G⁺/G⁻ under uniaxial strain). In GO the apparent G maximum often sits at 1590–1600 cm⁻¹ because it overlaps D′.
bands.diagnostics: Position + FWHM report doping and strain; pairing ω(G) with ω(2D) separates the two.

dispersion.source: not a double-resonance band in the atlas; treated as non-dispersive

fit.source: atlas plot.sig × 2.3548 — the atlas's schematic curve width, used only as a starting value for deconvolution (the atlas gives no measured FWHM)

bands.label: D′
bands.name: D′ band (D-prime)
bands.process: Intravalley double resonance: one in-plane longitudinal-optical (iLO) phonon plus a defect, connecting two points within the same Dirac cone around K. Appears as a shoulder on the high-frequency side of G.
bands.mechanism: Defect-activated companion to the D band. Because D (intervalley) and D′ (intravalley) probe different scattering geometries, their ratio encodes the physical nature of the defect.
bands.meaning: ID/ID′ classifies the dominant defect type (Eckmann 2012): ≈13 sp³ defects, ≈7 vacancies, ≈3.5 boundaries/edges.
bands.diagnostics: The single most useful ratio for distinguishing chemical (sp³) from structural (vacancy/edge) disorder.

dispersion.source: Intravalley double resonance (atlas D′ process); the atlas gives no dispersion rate.
dispersion.todo: Rate not in atlas. Window is widened instead of shifted (see matchDefaults.unknownDispersionAllowanceCmPerEV).

fit.source: atlas plot.sig × 2.3548 — the atlas's schematic curve width, used only as a starting value for deconvolution (the atlas gives no measured FWHM)

bands.label: 2D
bands.name: 2D band (G′)
bands.process: Two-phonon intervalley double resonance: two iTO phonons of opposite momentum (q and −q). It is the overtone of the D-band phonon, but the two phonons conserve momentum by themselves — so no defect is needed. Highly dispersive (~100 cm⁻¹/eV).
bands.mechanism: Because its intensity does not require disorder, the 2D band survives in pristine graphene where D is absent.
bands.meaning: In pristine single-layer graphene it is a single sharp Lorentzian (FWHM ≈ 24–30 cm⁻¹) with I2D/IG ≈ 2 (up to ~4 for suspended flakes). It splits into four components in AB-stacked bilayers and broadens with layer number. Re-emergence during GO reduction signals restored electronic conjugation.
bands.diagnostics: Lineshape + I<sub>2D</sub>/I<sub>G</sub> is the standard monolayer fingerprint; position also shifts with strain and doping.

fit.source: atlas plot.sig × 2.3548 — the atlas's schematic curve width, used only as a starting value for deconvolution (the atlas gives no measured FWHM)

bands.label: G*
bands.name: G* band (D+D″ / iTO+LA)
bands.process: Second-order intervalley combination of one in-plane transverse-optical (iTO / D-band) phonon and one longitudinal-acoustic (LA) phonon near the K point. Weak and only mildly dispersive.
bands.mechanism: A genuine graphene-lattice combination mode, also written D+D″ — where here “D″” means the ~1100 cm⁻¹ LA-branch phonon, not the ~1500 cm⁻¹ amorphous band. It is distinct from the ~2850–2920 cm⁻¹ window, which in oxidised GO is dominated by sp³ C–H stretching.
bands.meaning: A weak second-order feature centred near 2450 cm⁻¹. Your fits (2450–2550) and measured ~2459 sit right in range; the exact position is mildly excitation-dependent, so small left/right shifts are expected. Mainly a confirmation of an intact graphitic lattice.
bands.diagnostics: Presence confirms graphitic ordering; fit with a single Lorentzian and don’t over-interpret small shifts.
bands.correction: Fixed in this version. Earlier this atlas placed “D+D″” at ~2850–2900 cm⁻¹. The correct band — the one your data labels G* — is here at ~2450 cm⁻¹ (iTO+LA). The ~2850–2920 cm⁻¹ region is sp³ C–H stretching, not a phonon combination, so it is not a separate lattice band.

bands.label: D+D′
bands.name: D+D′ combination band
bands.use: Overall disorder; sp² recovery on reduction
bands.process: Disorder-activated combination of one D phonon (intervalley iTO) and one D′ phonon (intravalley iLO). Requires defects for momentum conservation.
bands.mechanism: Because it mixes the two defect channels, it is a robust overall measure of structural + chemical disorder.
bands.meaning: Its peak position correlates linearly with the % of sp² carbon recovered during GO reduction — one of the three correlations López-Díaz use to quantify oxidation degree.
bands.diagnostics: Position/area vs. sp² fraction; a practical reduction-progress meter.
bands.correction: Historically this band was mislabelled “D+G” (1350+1580 ≈ 2930). The correct assignment is D+D′ — the G phonon is Raman-allowed at Γ and does not participate in this double-resonance combination.

dispersion.source: D+D′ combination (atlas); the atlas gives no dispersion rate.

bands.label: 2D′
bands.name: 2D′ band (overtone of D′)
bands.process: Second-order overtone of D′: two intravalley iLO phonons. Like 2D, it needs no defect.
bands.mechanism: The intravalley counterpart of the 2D band, sitting at the high-frequency end of the spectrum.
bands.meaning: Responds to mechanical strain and is less sensitive to charge doping than G or 2D, which is why it has been proposed as an auxiliary gauge for strain assessment.
bands.diagnostics: Helpful as a cross-check when separating strain from doping — but combine with the ω(2D)–ω(G) correlation for a full separation.
bands.correction: Overstated in the source. 2D′ is not a “pure strain gauge free of doping.” Electrochemical-doping studies show its position/intensity do shift with carrier density; strain and charge effects remain coupled. It is less doping-sensitive than G/2D — useful, but not doping-independent (Del Corro 2015; Lee & Ryu 2012).

dispersion.source: Overtone of D′ (atlas); the atlas gives no dispersion rate.

ratios.b: The most-used ratio — but it is two-valued, so you must know the regime:
ratios.note: The ratio rises as defects increase, peaks near Lₐ ≈ 3–4 nm, then falls. A given I_D/I_G value maps to two crystallite sizes — disambiguate with G-band width (broad G ⇒ amorphisation regime).
Nearly excitation-independent, which makes it more robust than I_D/I_G for identifying what kind of defect dominates.

ratios.b: Read intensity ratio and lineshape together:
eqs: Single Lorentzian, FWHM ≈ 24–30 cm⁻¹, I_2D/I_G ≈ 2 → monolayer
4-component, broader 2D, lower ratio → AB bilayer / few-layer
Weak/absent 2D + strong D → GO / highly disordered
ratios.note: Suspended high-quality monolayers can reach I_2D/I_G ≈ 4. Substrate doping lowers the ratio, so combine with FWHM.

ratios.b: Integrated-area version used in GO work:
eqs: Compared against ab-initio curves for sp³ vs. vacancy defects
Position of 2D and of D+D′ → % sp² carbon (López-Díaz correlations)
ratios.note: Three independent correlations (I_D/I_G, ω(2D), ω(D+D′)) should agree — cross-check them and, where possible, against XPS C/O. Related practical metrics: G-band FWHM broadens with structural disorder, and the G/D area ratio scales with inter-defect distance L_D — the two metrics used in your spreadsheet.

ratios.b: An order gauge that explains a common surprise:
eqs: Ordered / graphitic (few defects): 2D strong & sharp → I(2D) > I(D+D′)
Highly oxidised / disordered GO: 2D weak & broad, combination bands grow → I(D+D′) > I(2D)
ratios.note: 2D needs no defect (two-phonon, momentum-conserved), so it collapses as oxidation rises while defect-activated D+D′ grows. If your 2D is stronger than the literature’s, your sample is less oxidised / more graphitic than theirs. Laser wavelength and layer number also shift these ratios.

workflow: Only G (~1585) + a single sharp 2D (FWHM < 30 cm⁻¹, I_2D/I_G ≥ 2), D absent → pristine single-layer graphene.
G + a broader, multi-component 2D, still little/no D → few-layer AB-stacked graphene (count components / check ratio).
Strong D, a D′ shoulder on G, broad bands, D* and D″ present, weak or absent 2D → graphene oxide / highly disordered carbon.
Compute I_D/I_D′ → 13 / 7 / 3.5 tells you sp³ vs. vacancy vs. edge defects.
Compute I_D/I_G, decide the regime from the G-band width, then apply the Cançado equation for crystallite size Lₐ.
Track reduction (GO→rGO): D/G evolving, 2D re-emerging, D+D′ shifting, and D*/D″ shrinking all indicate increasing sp² content.
For strain vs. doping: use ω(G) and ω(2D) positions and the ω(2D)-vs-ω(G) correlation; treat 2D′ as an auxiliary (not absolute) strain check.
Around 2850–2920 cm⁻¹, decide whether you are seeing a phonon combination or sp³ C–H stretching before assigning D+D″ — and remember the canonical D+D″/G* sits near 2450 cm⁻¹.
